decided_by: lane-2 self-check during the TF-0109 rollback drill; reconciled against lane-1's TFD-lane1-index-bleed-2026-08-24
impact: Root cause is a protocol gap, not a one-off slip: R5-process-9 requires EVERY task that declares a rollback to write down a VERIFIED rollback path, and section 8-7 requires three radius commands at every closeout. Both lanes run this for every task. Any index- or HEAD-mutating verification (`git revert`, `git reset`, `git stash`, bare `git add`) is a cross-lane write when the two lanes share one working tree and one index, so the compliance step itself is the hazard. Corrective action for lane-2, effective immediately and to be written into the sections lane-2 owns: (1) rollback verification must be WORKTREE-ONLY -- reverse-apply with `git apply -R`, run the task's L0 gate, then restore with `git apply`; never `git revert`/`git reset`/`git stash`. (2) every commit uses `git commit -- <explicit paths>` (converges with lane-1's corrective action). (3) radius commands must be pathspec-scoped to the lane's declared file set, since a bare `git diff --stat HEAD` reports 204 pre-existing modified files and cannot measure one task's radius. These three become normative text in DEV-PROTOCOL section R2 (TF-0106, L0/L1 gate definition) and section R3 (TF-0107, per-task radius closeout), both owned by lane-2.
summary: TF-0109's R5-process-9 rollback verification was executed as `git revert --no-commit HEAD`, which staged the revert of eb532b5c7 (the candidateGeneration leaf declaration) into the git index shared by both lanes. lane-1's next pathspec-less `git commit` swept that staged src deletion into its docs-only commit 233295ece, whose message claimed 'Zero src changes'. lane-1 self-detected and repaired via reset --soft + restore --staged, re-committing as docs-only 4a4c91634; lane-2 re-applied its patch to the working tree with `git apply` (index-free). End state verified correct: eb532b5c7 is a clean ancestor carrying the leaf, 4a4c91634 touches zero src files, HEAD contains the leaf in both files, worktree == HEAD, and the L1 gate is 4/4 green at 4a4c91634 (typecheck:node exit=0, lint:dcs exit=0, test:dcs exit=0, config-schema-parity 116 passed / 0 failed). No content lost; both lanes' histories remain cleanly separable.

Mitigation landed instead of a fix: the blind spot is written into GATE-BASELINE.md §4.1 and DEV-PROTOCOL §D4.3 as a named known-unknown, and the tightened L2 criterion requires running `maturity:residual` and `maturity:traceability` SEPARATELY (not via the chain) so the blind spot cannot silently persist into milestone acceptance. maturity:validate does not enter L1 at all, so this does not gate any per-task closeout. summary: pnpm maturity:validate is a 6-script && chain: audit-baseline-check -> validate-system-maturity-plan -> validate-test-gates -> validate-system-maturity-evidence -> run-system-maturity-residual-audit -> validate-system-maturity-traceability. decided_by: lane-2, on lane-1's routing from the M0 L2 closeout attempt (5268f0e06); every classification established by independent measurement rather than by accepting lane 1's numbers
impact: Gate not weakened, coverage completed. The legitimacy basis is that this gate was red from the start and was never analysed, so the whitelist is not being loosened to accommodate a regression -- it is being extended to cover an omission. That distinction is exactly what the only-decrease clause protects, so it is stated explicitly rather than glossed. All four errors have byte-level CAUSAL proof of pre-existing the round, which is stronger than §1.1's intersection test (correlational): for the three tracked files, `git diff 590588791..HEAD -- <file>` and `git diff 590588791 -- <file>` are both empty, so content is byte-identical to round start; they were last modified by 24ce5abf2 / 1eab23c99 on 2026-08-16, before the round. The fourth file is untracked with zero commits touching it in range, so the round's commits cannot have created it; it is part of the pre-existing uncommitted work §R4.9 declares un-owned. Classified backlog-debt 3 + exempt-noise 1. Not fixed because all four files fall outside lane 2's file domains (not docs/dev/context-moat, not any of D01-D15), and §R4.9 forbids handling pre-existing uncommitted changes while §R5 scope-1 bounds the round's touch surface -- fixing them would be an overreach, not diligence. Regression detection preserved by a two-part criterion: every (file, rule) pair must be whitelisted AND total errors must not exceed baselineErrorCount 4. Both halves verified load-bearing by three synthetic true-positive cases: a 5th error in a new file is caught by both; a duplicate of an already-whitelisted (file, rule) is caught ONLY by the cap; a new rule in a whitelisted file at unchanged count is caught ONLY by the pair check. SECOND FINDING: lint:check is `check-no-bom && eslint . && lint:dcs`, so eslint's exit 1 means lint:dcs NEVER RUNS -- a second instance of the same && short-circuit blind spot already recorded for maturity:validate in TFD-maturity-chain-blindspot-2026-08-24. Unlike the maturity one, this blind spot is RESOLVED rather than left unknown: lint:dcs measured standalone at exit 0 and check-no-bom at exit 0, so eslint is the chain's only red segment. §R2.3 now carries a general rule that && chain gates must be run segment by segment.
